key: A kirana shop has two helpers. One is th
name: ch00_kirana_sorter_talker
alt: A kirana shop with a silent helper sorting goods onto shelves and a chatty helper talking to a customer and writing the bill.
scene: A wide, eye-level view into a small, crowded Indian kirana shop, open to the street, with steel shelves rising to the ceiling and gunny sacks of rice and dal on the floor. On the LEFT, a lean young helper (about 20, grey vest, cotton towel over his shoulder, sleeves rolled) stands with his back half-turned, silently placing a packet of rice on the rice shelf with one hand while his other hand already reaches for a bar of soap; a neat trail of curved arrows shows each item flying from an open carton to its correct shelf section marked only by small picture icons of a rice grain, a soap bar and a snack packet. His lips are closed and his face is calm and focused. On the RIGHT, behind a glass-topped wooden counter with a jar of toffees and a small weighing scale, a cheerful chubby helper in his 30s (striped half-sleeve shirt, pen behind his ear) leans forward laughing with a middle-aged woman customer in a green salwar kameez holding a cloth bag; a speech bubble rises from him and he is writing on a long paper bill with a ballpoint. Both helpers wear the same shop apron to hint that they are built from the same stuff. Warm late-morning sunlight spills in from the street. Labels: "REPRESENTATION" in a small tag directly above the silent sorter, "GENERATIVE" in a tag directly above the talking helper at the counter.

key: A tailor altering a ready-made kurta. Th
name: ch00_tailor_kurta_alteration
alt: A tailor shortening the sleeves of a ready-made kurta for a customer, while an untouched bolt of cloth and a loom sit unused in the corner.
scene: A cosy, slightly elevated three-quarter view inside a small Indian tailoring shop with a wooden cutting table, a black treadle sewing machine and shelves of folded fabric. In the centre, an elderly tailor (about 60, white kurta-pyjama, round spectacles low on his nose, measuring tape around his neck) pins the sleeve of a cream ready-made kurta worn by a young man in his mid-20s who stands with arms held out, the sleeves visibly too long and covering his hands. A chalk line on the sleeve marks where it will be cut, and a pair of big tailor's scissors lies ready on the table beside a pincushion. On the wall hangs a finished kurta on a hanger with a small paper tag reading "90%". In the back-left corner, half in shadow and covered in a dusty sheet, sits an old handloom with an untouched roll of raw cloth; a faint dashed circle with a diagonal strike-through floats over it to show this route is not needed. A narrow inset bubble near the young man's wrist shows the before and after sleeve length with a small curved arrow. Soft warm light from a single bulb and a street window, a calm, friendly mood. Labels: "PRETRAINED" on a tag hanging from the kurta's collar, "FINE-TUNING" on a small banner above the tailor's scissors, "FROM SCRATCH" on the dusty sheet over the loom.

key: word2vec learns meaning the way you lear
name: ch01_canteen_friend_groups
alt: A new employee in an office canteen noticing which colleagues always sit together, with dotted lines grouping them in his head.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated view of a bright Indian office canteen at lunchtime, rows of long tables with steel tiffin boxes, plates of rice and dal, and a counter with a big tea urn in the background. In the foreground right, a new employee (late 20s, crisp light-blue shirt, ID card on a lanyard, holding a tray with a plate and a glass of buttermilk) stands still and watches the room with a curious, thoughtful expression. Across the room three clear groups sit at separate tables: four young engineers in hoodies laughing over laptops, three accountants in formal shirts with calculators beside their plates, and a group of women from sales in bright kurtas sharing food from one tiffin. Above the new employee's head floats a large thought bubble showing a simple scatter of small round face icons, the same three groups clustered into tight little islands with distance between islands, with faint dashed lines linking each canteen table to its island in the bubble. No one is talking to the new employee; he is only observing who sits with whom. Warm midday light through tall windows, relaxed bustling mood. Labels: "CONTEXT" in a small tag on the middle table, "EMBEDDING SPACE" inside the top edge of the thought bubble.

key: An RNN is a relay race: the baton (hidde
name: ch01_relay_vs_group_chat
alt: Split image: a relay race where a baton must pass runner to runner, versus a group of people who all post and read each other's messages at once.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a dusty school athletics track seen from the side, four runners in matching red vests in a single line, each waiting in turn; the first, a sweaty teenage boy, stretches to hand a silver baton to the second, while the third and fourth stand idle with hands on knees, clearly unable to start until the baton arrives. A long curved arrow runs strictly from runner one to runner four, one hop at a time, and a small stopwatch icon floats above it. RIGHT panel: the same four young people now sit in a circle on a lawn, each holding a phone, and above them float four chat bubbles posted at the same moment; thin crisscrossing lines connect every bubble to every person, showing everyone reading everyone else at once, their faces lit up and engaged. In the lower corner of the right panel, a small inset shows a quiz sheet with the top two answers visible and the lower answers covered by a sheet of paper, a hand peeking at only the earlier lines. Bright outdoor daylight, energetic mood. Labels: "RNN" at the top of the left panel, "TRANSFORMER" at the top of the right panel, "MASK" beside the covered quiz sheet inset.

key: Pretraining is 12 years of school: years
name: ch01_school_then_courses
alt: A school building graduate stepping out onto three paths leading to short courses for a bank clerk, a call-centre agent and other jobs.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of a long journey laid out from left to right. On the far LEFT stands a large, old cream-coloured school building with a tall clock tower and a huge stack of books beside the gate, students in white-and-navy uniforms streaming in; a tall banner of years marked simply "12 YEARS" runs along its wall. From its gate walks a confident young graduate (about 18, white shirt, school tie loosened, backpack) carrying a rolled certificate. In front of him the road forks into three short, narrow paths, each leading to a small single-room coaching institute: one with a bank counter and a ledger in the window, one with headsets on desks, one with a stethoscope poster. Above each small building is a calendar showing just three months. Ghosted copies of the same graduate walk down each path at once, as if he has been duplicated, each copy wearing a different work outfit at the end: a bank clerk with a tie, a call-centre agent with a headset, a clinic assistant in a blue coat. Near the bank clerk, a manager with a clipboard gives a thumbs-up speech bubble for on-the-job feedback. Clear morning light, hopeful mood. Labels: "PRETRAINING" over the school building, "FINE-TUNING" over the three small institutes, "ALIGNMENT" beside the manager with the clipboard.

key: VRAM is the size of the kitchen counter
name: ch01_dhaba_counter_vram
alt: A dhaba cook at a small counter crammed with ingredients, with a helper chopping and packing ingredients smaller so they fit.
scene: A close, slightly elevated three-quarter view into a roadside Indian dhaba kitchen at night, lit by a hanging bulb and the blue glow of a gas burner. In the centre, a burly cook in his 40s (white vest, red checked towel on his shoulder, moustache) stands at a narrow steel counter that is completely overflowing: whole cauliflowers, heaps of onions, a sack of potatoes and big bunches of coriander spill over the edges and tumble toward the floor, and he looks frustrated with his hands raised because there is no room to cook. A big kadai sits on the stove waiting. Down a corridor in the background, through an open door, a large dim storeroom with shelves full of sacks is visible, far away. On the right side, a young helper (about 18, cap, apron) sits on a stool chopping vegetables into tiny cubes and packing them into small steel boxes; a curved arrow shows the small boxes going onto the counter, where they now fit neatly in a tidy row. A small inset bubble next to the helper shows one big onion turning into a small compact box, with a tiny note under it reading "4-bit". Warm, busy, humid atmosphere. Labels: "VRAM" on the front edge of the steel counter, "QUANTIZATION" above the helper with the small boxes, "RAM" over the faraway storeroom door.

key: A kirana shopkeeper billing a list: "2 P
name: ch02_kirana_barcode_split
alt: A kirana shopkeeper billing items: common items are scanned as one barcode each while an unusual pickle jar is written as three separate entries.
scene: A close, eye-level view across the glass counter of a busy Indian kirana shop, shelves of colourful packets and jars behind. The shopkeeper (about 50, sleeveless sweater over a white shirt, reading glasses, bindi of sandalwood on the forehead) holds a handheld barcode scanner. On the counter to the left, two familiar items, a packet of biscuits and a block of butter, each have a single clear barcode, and a short beam from the scanner turns each into one neat entry on the long paper bill rolling out of a small printer. In the centre sits an unusual glass jar of homemade pickle with a hand-drawn label and no barcode at all; a puzzled question mark floats above it. To the right, the shopkeeper has written the jar on the bill as three separate short lines, and three small curved arrows lead from three parts of the jar (its brand sticker, the type of pickle, the size printed on the lid) to those three bill lines. A young customer (college student, hoodie, cloth bag) watches with mild amusement. Bright tubelight, warm everyday mood. Labels: "ONE TOKEN" beside the biscuit packet's single bill line, "SUBWORD PIECES" beside the three bill lines for the pickle, "TOKENIZER" on a small sticker on the scanner.

key: Packing a tiffin for a long train journe
name: ch02_tiffin_compartments
alt: Three tiffin carriers on a train berth compared: whole dishes, single grains, and mixable portions.
scene: A slightly elevated three-quarter view inside an Indian train sleeper compartment with blue berths and a window showing passing green fields. On the lower berth sit three open steel tiffin carriers side by side, each with four stacked round compartments opened out in a row. LEFT tiffin: each compartment holds one complete dish (a full biryani, a full paneer curry, a full kheer, a full dosa), but a hungry passenger leaning in asks for something else and a small speech bubble shows a bowl of rajma with a red cross, meaning it was never packed. MIDDLE tiffin: each compartment holds just one single grain of rice, almost empty, looking absurd and wasteful. RIGHT tiffin: compartments hold flexible portions (rice, dal, a bit of pickle, chopped onion) and a small arrow shows them combining on a steel plate into rajma-chawal and other new meals, a satisfied smile on the passenger's face. The passenger is a middle-aged man in a half-sleeve shirt and lungi, sitting cross-legged; an elderly co-passenger in a shawl looks on from the opposite berth. Soft morning light streaming through the barred window, gentle rocking-train mood. Labels: "WORDS" above the left tiffin, "CHARACTERS" above the middle tiffin, "SUBWORDS" above the right tiffin.

key: The word "bat" in a dictionary has one e
name: ch02_bat_contextual_meaning
alt: A dictionary listing every meaning of bat, compared with a cricket commentator meaning a cricket bat and a costume party where it means the animal.
scene: A three-part composition, read left to right. LEFT: an open, thick dictionary lying on a wooden desk, one entry circled, with two small icons drawn in the margin next to the word, a cricket bat and a flying bat animal, both shown equally, representing one fixed entry for every meaning. CENTRE: a cricket commentary box high above a floodlit stadium, a commentator in his 50s (blazer, headset microphone, excited open mouth, one arm raised) shouting toward the pitch where a batter in white has just hit the ball; a speech bubble from him shows only an image of a cricket bat, glowing. RIGHT: a costume party in a dim, decorated living room with orange paper lanterns and fake cobwebs, a young woman in a black cape pointing up at a small furry bat hanging upside down from the ceiling fan, her friends laughing; her speech bubble shows only the animal. Thin arrows from the words around each speaker (stadium, crowd, ball on one side; lanterns, cobwebs on the other) flow into each bubble to show that the surrounding context picks the meaning. Lighting: neutral daylight on the dictionary, bright floodlights in the centre, warm orange glow on the right. Labels: "STATIC" above the dictionary, "CONTEXTUAL" spanning the centre and right scenes.

key: In a Mumbai local, people who board at t
name: ch02_local_train_regulars
alt: A Mumbai local train compartment where regular commuters who board at the same times cluster into groups: office-goers, students, vendors.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view down the length of a crowded Mumbai suburban train compartment in the morning rush, yellow-and-maroon interior, open doors with the platform blurring past, overhead grab handles swaying. Three natural clusters of regular commuters occupy different zones. Near the left door, office-goers in formal shirts and lanyards stand close together, holding laptop bags and folded newspapers, chatting. In the centre, a lively group of college students with backpacks and earphones share one phone screen and laugh. Near the right door, two vendors sit on the floor with a basket of guavas and a tray of hairclips, sharing a joke. Over each cluster hovers a soft translucent coloured circle, like islands on a map, with a small pin at the centre. In the foreground, a curious observer (young woman, late 20s, kurta and denim jacket, holding a pole) glances from group to group, and a thought bubble near her shows a mini map with the three islands placed close or far apart. A tiny inset in the top corner shows four small crown and throne icons grouped together on the same kind of map. Bright morning sun cutting through the doors, busy but friendly mood. Labels: "SAME COMPANY" above the students, "CLOSE VECTORS" inside the observer's thought bubble.

key: Antakshari (the song chain game) played
name: ch03_antakshari_no_memory
alt: A man with no memory sings one word of a song at a time, while a friend re-reads him the whole song so far each round.
scene: A cosy, eye-level view of an Indian living room on a festive evening, string lights along the window and family members sitting on a carpet in a loose circle for antakshari. In the centre sits a cheerful man in his 40s (kurta, slightly confused but game expression); a thought bubble above his head is completely empty, a small eraser drawn inside it. Kneeling beside him, his niece (about 16, ponytail, glasses) holds a long scroll of paper on which the song so far is written, and she is reading it aloud to him from the very first line, her finger tracing the text. The man sings out one single word, shown as a small music-note bubble, and a curved arrow carries that word back to the bottom of the scroll where it is being added in fresh ink. A circular looping arrow around the pair shows this repeats: read everything, add one word, read everything again. The scroll is visibly getting longer and piling up on the floor. Other relatives clap and laugh around them; a harmonium sits to one side. Warm golden lamp light, playful mood. Labels: "WHOLE PROMPT" on the long scroll, "ONE TOKEN" next to the single sung word, "LOOP" beside the circular arrow.

key: A kirana shop's running khata (credit no
name: ch03_khata_kv_cache
alt: Split image: a shopkeeper re-adding a month of bills versus simply adding today's item to a running total in his khata notebook.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, the same small kirana shop counter and the same shopkeeper (about 55, white kurta, Gandhi cap, grey moustache) in both halves, with a regular customer (young mother with a toddler on her hip) waiting with one packet of milk. LEFT panel: the shopkeeper is buried under a messy pile of thirty crumpled paper bills, sweating, running his finger down each one and tapping a big calculator, a long queue of impatient customers forming behind the mother; a tall stack icon shows the same work being redone. RIGHT panel: he calmly opens a thick red cloth-bound khata notebook, the page showing a neat running column of numbers, and simply writes one new line at the bottom, smiling, the customer already turning to leave. A small inset next to the khata shows the notebook slowly getting thicker with every visit, pages bulging, a hint that the record keeps growing. Late afternoon light through the shutter, warm and familiar. Labels: "RECOMPUTE" at the top of the left panel, "KV CACHE" at the top of the right panel, "GROWS" next to the bulging-notebook inset.

key: In a WhatsApp family group, someone writ
name: ch03_family_chat_scroll_up
alt: A woman reads 'Did he reach?' in a family group chat and scrolls up to find who was travelling, with glowing links back to earlier messages.
scene: A close, slightly over-the-shoulder view of a woman in her early 30s (simple cotton saree, hair in a loose bun, sitting on a sofa with a cup of tea) looking at her phone, which is shown enlarged and floating beside her so the chat is clearly visible. The screen shows a generic family group chat with plain green and white bubbles and tiny round avatars. At the bottom, the newest message reads "Did he reach?" with the word "he" highlighted. Above it, earlier messages are only shown as short grey lines except one, near the top, which carries a small train icon and an avatar of a young man with a backpack. From the highlighted "he", several curved glowing lines of different thickness reach upward to earlier bubbles: the thickest line connects to the train message, thinner lines touch other messages, showing that every earlier message gets some weight but one matters most. Her thumb is mid-scroll upward, and her expression changes from puzzled to understanding. A ceiling fan and a framed family photo are visible in the background. Soft evening lamp light, calm domestic mood. Labels: "QUERY" next to the highlighted word, "ATTENTION" along the thickest glowing line, "EARLIER TOKENS" beside the stack of older bubbles.

key: Cooking in a tiny kitchen (SRAM) with a
name: ch03_flash_attention_kitchen
alt: Split image: a cook making many trips to a far storeroom versus a cook who brings one tray, finishes all its steps, then returns once.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same tiny kitchen on the left side of the frame and a large storeroom far down a long corridor on the right. LEFT panel: a harried cook in his 30s (white apron, cap askew, sweat drops) runs back and forth along the corridor carrying a single onion, then a single bowl, then a pan; many footprint trails and a tangle of back-and-forth arrows fill the corridor, and a wall clock shows a lot of time gone. The tiny kitchen counter is almost empty. RIGHT panel: a calm cook of the same age carries one full steel tray from the storeroom into the tiny kitchen, then on the counter we see the tray being chopped, mixed and cooked in a quick sequence of three small numbered steps, and finally he walks back only once with a finished, steaming dish on a plate; just two clean arrows mark the corridor. A small inset bubble at the bottom shows both final dishes are exactly the same, with an equals sign between them. Bright functional kitchen light, slightly comic tone on the left and serene on the right. Labels: "SRAM" over the tiny kitchen, "HBM" over the storeroom door, "FLASH ATTENTION" at the top of the right panel.

key: Sorting letters at a post office. A repr
name: ch04_sorting_machine_vs_clerk
alt: Split image: a post-office sorting machine dropping letters into fixed numbered bins versus a chatty clerk explaining in a sentence which bin a letter belongs to.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, inside the same large Indian post office with red walls and wooden pigeon-hole racks. LEFT panel: a boxy grey sorting machine with a conveyor belt and a scanning window; letters slide in and drop with mechanical precision into three metal bins numbered 1, 2 and 3 below it, small motion lines showing each letter falling straight down. No person speaks; the machine's indicator light glows steadily. RIGHT panel: a friendly postal clerk in his 40s (khaki uniform, spectacles, pen tucked in pocket) sits at a wooden desk holding one letter up to the light, leaning toward a young woman customer and talking; a large speech bubble from him contains a small drawing of bin 1 with a tiny question mark beside bin 2, showing a hedged, chatty answer. Behind him, a freshly hand-painted new bin with a blank label stands next to the old ones, showing he can sort into a category that did not exist yesterday. On the clerk's desk sits a small funnel turning his speech bubble into a single clean number tag. Daylight through high windows, calm institutional mood. Labels: "REPRESENTATION MODEL" at the top of the left panel, "GENERATIVE MODEL" at the top of the right panel, "PARSER" beside the funnel.

key: A fishing net. Recall: of all the fish i
name: ch04_fishing_net_precision_recall
alt: A fisherman's big net hauled from a lake full of fish and junk, showing how many fish it caught and how much rubbish came with it.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of a calm village lake at dawn with a small wooden boat near the shore. Two fishermen (one older, about 60, white vest and checked lungi, grey stubble; one younger, about 25, rolled-up trousers and a cap) haul an enormous net onto the muddy bank. The net is bulging: it holds many silver fish but also a pile of rubbish, two old rubber chappals, a plastic bottle, a broken bucket and some weeds, and the younger man holds up one chappal with a grimace. In the water behind them, the lake is drawn partly cut-away so we can see a few fish still swimming free outside the net. On the left of the bank, a small chalkboard propped on a stick shows two simple pie-like circles: one comparing caught fish to all fish in the lake, the other comparing fish to everything in the net. A small inset bubble in the top corner shows a tiny precise hand-net holding only two fish and nothing else, for contrast. Soft pink-orange morning light with mist on the water, quiet, slightly humorous mood. Labels: "RECALL" above the fish still visible in the lake, "PRECISION" beside the pile of rubbish in the net, "F1" on the small chalkboard.

key: A wholesale mandi grades mangoes. A mach
name: ch04_mandi_mango_grader
alt: At a mango mandi, a fixed measuring machine reads each mango and a junior grader learns to draw a straight line splitting export-quality from the rest.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of a busy wholesale fruit mandi under a corrugated tin roof, wooden crates of golden mangoes stacked everywhere. On the LEFT stands a large old steel measuring machine bolted to the floor with a padlock on its side panel; mangoes roll along a short conveyor through it and out the other side, each with a small paper slip printed with a long row of tiny numbers. In the CENTRE, a young junior grader (about 22, cotton shirt, pencil behind his ear, eager expression) sits at a wooden table spreading out these slips on a large sheet of chart paper, where the mangoes appear as dots; he is drawing one straight ruler line across the dots, with the dots above the line coloured gold and below it coloured green. Behind him, two senior graders (elderly men in white kurtas and turbans) point approvingly, holding mangoes they had already sorted into crates marked by coloured stickers. On the RIGHT, finished crates with a small airplane sticker go onto a truck. Late-afternoon sun slanting through gaps in the roof, dusty golden light, busy trading mood. Labels: "FROZEN EMBEDDING" on the padlocked machine, "CLASSIFIER" next to the ruler line, "LABELS" above the senior graders' crates.

key: Asking a very knowledgeable but chatty u
name: ch04_chatty_uncle_one_word
alt: Split image: a chatty uncle giving a long speech about an essay versus answering 'Pass' in one word when asked a precise question.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, the same living room and the same knowledgeable uncle (about 65, white kurta, shawl, thick-rimmed spectacles, holding a handwritten essay) sitting in a wooden armchair in both halves, and the same teenage nephew (about 15, school uniform) standing beside him. LEFT panel: the nephew asks with an open hand gesture and a speech bubble showing only a question mark; the uncle is in full flow, one finger raised, a gigantic winding speech bubble filling the whole top of the panel with scribbled lines, a wall clock showing that ten minutes have passed, and the nephew is yawning and slumping. RIGHT panel: the nephew holds up a small card with a crisp printed question, and the uncle answers with a tiny, neat speech bubble containing the single word "Pass", smiling; the nephew is giving a thumbs-up, and the essay now has a clean tick on it. On a side table in both panels sits the same stack of books, showing the uncle's knowledge is unchanged. Warm afternoon light through lace curtains, gently humorous mood. Labels: "VAGUE PROMPT" at the top of the left panel, "CLEAR PROMPT" at the top of the right panel.

key: A raddiwala (scrap dealer) gets a truck
name: ch05_raddiwala_piles
alt: A scrap dealer sorting a truckload of mixed paper into piles of newspapers, cardboard and notebooks, then writing a price label on each pile.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of an Indian raddiwala's open yard under a tarpaulin sheet. On the left, a small tempo truck has just tipped out a huge unlabelled heap of mixed paper: newspapers, cardboard boxes, school notebooks, magazines and a few odd items. In the centre, the raddiwala (about 50, faded blue shirt, towel on his head against the sun, sturdy and cheerful) is mid-motion, tossing a bundle of newspapers onto a growing pile, with curved arrows showing items flying from the heap to three neat piles: a stack of tied newspapers, a stack of flattened cardboard, a stack of notebooks. Off to one side, a small messy heap holds a broken umbrella, a calendar and a shoe box. On the right, his teenage son (about 15, t-shirt, slippers) sticks a hand-written cardboard sign onto the newspaper pile reading "NEWSPAPER", with a chalk price drawn as a coin icon. A large hanging balance scale dangles from a beam. Hot, bright midday sunlight with sharp shadows, honest working mood. Labels: "CLUSTERING" above the three neat piles, "OUTLIERS" beside the small odd heap, "TOPIC LABEL" beside the son's sign.

key: k-means is a school principal who says "
name: ch05_houses_vs_college_fest
alt: Split image: a principal assigning every student to one of three houses versus a college fest where groups form naturally and a loner stands alone by the chai stall.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a school assembly ground, a stern principal in her 50s (cotton saree, spectacles, clipboard) points firmly at three coloured flag posts, red, blue and green, with exactly three lines of students in uniform beneath them; one shy new boy with an oversized bag is being gently pushed by a teacher into the blue line, looking lost. A big "3" is painted on the principal's clipboard. RIGHT panel: a lively college fest at dusk with fairy lights, a dance group rehearsing in one corner, a band jamming with guitars in another, a group of coders around a laptop on the steps, each group naturally clumped together with soft glowing outlines around them. Far from all the groups, beside a small chai stall with a steaming kettle, a lone student in a hoodie sips tea, perfectly content, with no outline around him. Bright morning light on the left panel, warm festive evening light on the right. Labels: "K-MEANS" at the top of the left panel, "HDBSCAN" at the top of the right panel, "OUTLIER" beside the lone student at the chai stall.

key: A thali. The plate (pipeline) has fixed
name: ch05_thali_katoris_pipeline
alt: A steel thali with fixed katoris, one katori being swapped from paneer to aloo while the rest of the meal stays the same.
scene: A top-down, slightly angled close view of a large round steel thali on a banana-leaf-green tablecloth in a simple Indian restaurant. The thali has five small steel katoris arranged in a fixed arc: yellow dal, a sabzi, white rice, a stack of rotis and a small sweet. Each katori sits in its own pressed circular slot in the plate. A waiter's hand in a white sleeve enters from the right, lifting out the sabzi katori filled with paneer curry and lowering a replacement katori of aloo curry into the exact same slot; a curved swap arrow links the two. The other four katoris remain untouched, with little check marks floating beside them. At the top edge of the frame, a customer (young man, late 20s, office shirt) looks on, already tearing a roti. In a small inset bubble at the bottom corner, a different katori is being swapped and a small round dish labelled with a minus sign disappears, hinting that some swaps change what comes later. Warm overhead restaurant light, appetising and orderly mood. Labels: "PIPELINE" on the rim of the thali, "SWAPPABLE STEP" next to the swap arrow, "BERTOPIC" on a small tag tucked under the plate.

key: A wedding photographer's assistant group
name: ch05_wedding_photo_albums
alt: A wedding photographer's assistant sorts thousands of photos into albums with keyword tags, and the photographer writes a title for each album.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view inside a small photo studio. On the left, a young assistant (about 23, t-shirt, glasses, focused) sits at a long table covered with thousands of printed wedding photos, sliding them into a row of open albums; curved arrows show photos going into the right album, and each album has a small sticky tag of three keywords drawn as tiny icons (henna hands and green leaves on one, a fire pit and garlands on another, a dance floor on a third). On the right, the senior photographer (a woman in her 40s, kurta with a camera strap around her neck, reading glasses) sits at a desk with just four of the best photos from one album fanned out in front of her, writing an elegant title on the album's cover with a fountain pen; the cover reads "Mehendi, Day 1". Behind her, a shelf already holds a neat row of titled albums. A small counter-style badge near the assistant shows a big pile marked "5000", and one near the photographer shows "30". Warm studio lamps and soft window light, calm creative mood. Labels: "CLUSTERS" above the assistant's albums, "C-TF-IDF" on the keyword tags, "LLM LABEL" beside the photographer's pen.

key: A cricket captain setting the batting or
name: ch06_captain_temperature
alt: A cricket captain picking the batting order: by the book in a Test final, and sending a tail-ender in at No. 3 in a fun exhibition match.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, the same cricket captain (about 30, team blazer over whites, cap, holding a clipboard batting order) in a dressing room in both halves. LEFT panel: a serious Test-match dressing room with white kits, a trophy in a glass case and a tense coach looking on; the captain's clipboard shows a neat, numbered top order in a straight column, each name matched to a batter sitting in sequence on the bench, padded up, unsmiling; a small thermometer icon on the wall is nearly empty and blue. RIGHT panel: a colourful T20 exhibition dressing room with music and coloured jerseys; the captain grins and points at a burly tail-ender with a fast bowler's build who is surprised but excited, strapping on pads to go in at number 3, while teammates laugh and cheer; the clipboard shows the order scrambled with a looping arrow; the thermometer on the wall is nearly full and red. A tiny inset in the lower right shows a chain of small dice rolling one after another, hinting that randomness happens at every step. Bright stadium light through windows. Labels: "LOW TEMPERATURE" at the top of the left panel, "HIGH TEMPERATURE" at the top of the right panel.

key: Ordering a custom cake at a bakery: pers
name: ch06_custom_cake_order
alt: A customer briefs a baker on a custom anniversary cake, with each part of the brief shown as a separate card on the counter.
scene: A warm, eye-level view across the glass counter of a small Indian neighbourhood bakery, trays of puffs and pastries in the display below and shelves of cake boxes behind. On the right, a young woman in her late 20s (kurti and jeans, tote bag, enthusiastic) leans in and lays out a row of small paper cards on the counter, one by one, like a hand of playing cards; each card carries a simple picture: a baker's toque for the role, a cake outline for the task, two wedding rings with the number 25 for the occasion, a two-tier round cake sketch for the format, a small child's face for the audience, an elegant swirl for the tone, and two hearts with initials "A & R". On the left, the baker (about 45, white chef's coat and cap, flour on his forearms) studies the cards carefully, nodding, pen poised over an order book. Above him floats a thought bubble showing the finished elegant two-tier cake. In a small inset at the bottom corner, the same baker stares at a single card with only the cake outline, and his thought bubble shows a random cartoonish cake with a question mark, showing what happens when parts are missing. Soft golden shop light, friendly, organised mood. Labels: "PROMPT COMPONENTS" above the row of cards, "OUTPUT" beside the thought-bubble cake.

key: Asking three auto drivers at the station
name: ch06_three_auto_drivers
alt: A traveller asks three auto-rickshaw drivers for the same fare; two say 180 and one says 400, and he goes with the majority.
scene: A wide, eye-level view of a busy Indian railway station forecourt in the evening, with a row of three green-and-yellow auto-rickshaws parked at the kerb and the station's arched entrance glowing behind. A traveller (about 30, rolling suitcase, backpack, office shirt, slightly tired) stands in the foreground facing the drivers. Each driver leans out of his auto with a speech bubble: the first (about 50, khaki uniform, grey moustache) says "180", the second (younger, about 25, cap, chewing) also says "180", and the third (about 40, sunglasses on his head, a sly grin) says "400". Above the traveller floats a simple tally board with two marks under 180 and one under 400, and a bold tick beside 180. He is pointing toward the first auto, about to get in. A faint overcast cloud with light drizzle hangs over the far right corner of the scene, hinting that all three could share the same bias if it rained. Warm sodium streetlights, bustling but resolved mood. Labels: "SELF-CONSISTENCY" above the tally board, "SAMPLES" along the row of three speech bubbles, "MAJORITY VOTE" beside the tick.

key: An exam with OMR sheets. The student can
name: ch06_omr_sheet_constraints
alt: A student filling an OMR exam sheet where only bubbles A, B, C or D can be shaded, with an unused free-text thought drifting away.
scene: A close, slightly elevated view over the shoulder of a teenage student (about 17, white school shirt, hair neatly combed, pencil in hand) sitting at a wooden exam desk in a large hall with rows of other students and a ceiling fan turning. On the desk lies a large OMR answer sheet with rows of empty circles labelled only A, B, C and D, and the student is carefully shading one bubble dark with an HB pencil. Above the student's head, a thought bubble holds a flowery long word scribbled with stars, as if she wants to write something expressive, but a dotted arrow from it hits the edge of the OMR sheet and bounces off, with a small barrier line, because there is no space to write anything except bubbles. Beside the sheet, a small dice icon with a pencil shows that which bubble gets shaded is still a choice. In the background, an invigilator in a cotton saree walks between the rows holding a stack of papers. In a small inset in the corner, a correctly filled sheet with a perfectly valid but wrong bubble is marked with a gentle question mark. Bright, even exam-hall light, quiet, focused mood. Labels: "CONSTRAINED SAMPLING" above the OMR sheet, "VALID FORMAT" beside the shaded bubble, "TEMPERATURE" next to the dice icon.

key: Your phone's photo gallery. A RAW photo
name: ch07_photo_quantization
alt: A phone photo of a family shown at four sizes, from a large sharp version down to a tiny blurry thumbnail where faces smear.
scene: A clean, front-on view of a wooden table with a smartphone lying in the centre, and above it four floating copies of the same cheerful family photo arranged in a descending row from left to right. The photo shows three generations at a temple courtyard: a grandmother in a white saree, parents in festive clothes and two small kids grinning. The LEFT copy is huge, crisp and detailed, every thread on the saree visible, with a heavy file icon beneath it. The second copy is noticeably smaller and still looks almost identical. The third is smaller again and still clear. The RIGHT copy is a tiny square thumbnail where the faces have smeared into blocky blurs and the kids' smiles are lost. Below each copy sits a small storage box whose size shrinks from big to tiny, with arrows showing the shrink. A young man (about 25, t-shirt, curious) leans over the table squinting at the tiny one. In a small inset in the lower right corner, a long chain of tiny multiplication signs shows small errors adding up step by step. Soft daylight from a window, clean and clear mood. Labels: "16-BIT" under the large photo, "4-BIT" under the third photo, "2-BIT" under the tiny blurry thumbnail.

key: A government office where a different cl
name: ch07_carry_your_own_file
alt: At a government office, a citizen places his own thick file folder on a new clerk's desk so the clerk can read his whole case.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view inside an old Indian government office: high ceiling, slow ceiling fan, peeling green walls, steel cupboards and stacks of dusty files tied with red ribbon. A long row of four identical wooden desks recedes into the background, each with a different clerk (an elderly man with spectacles, a young woman in a saree, a middle-aged man with a moustache, a bored young man), suggesting a different clerk serves you on every visit. In the foreground, a patient citizen in his 40s (half-sleeve checked shirt, plastic carry bag) sets a thick buff-coloured file folder down on the nearest desk with both hands; the folder bulges with pages and has a small stack of numbered visit slips sticking out. The clerk opens it with a slightly weary face. A gauge drawn on the side of the desk shows how thick the folder can get before it overflows, with a red zone at the top. A small dashed arrow from the citizen's bag to the desk is labelled with a calendar showing repeated visits. Dusty afternoon sunlight through tall barred windows, slow bureaucratic mood. Labels: "STATELESS LLM" above the row of clerks, "MEMORY" on the bulging folder, "CONTEXT WINDOW" beside the gauge.

key: Minutes of a society committee meeting.
name: ch07_committee_minutes
alt: A housing-society secretary keeps short running minutes of committee meetings, while a resident asks exactly what someone said about the parking fee.
scene: A wide, eye-level view of a small housing-society meeting room with plastic chairs in a semicircle, a whiteboard and a notice board with circulars. On the left, faded and ghost-like in the background, a tall stack of ten previous meetings' full transcripts towers on a side table, thick and unread, covered in a thin layer of dust. In the centre, the society secretary (woman in her 50s, cotton saree, reading glasses on a chain, calm and efficient) sits at a folding table writing in a slim register of running minutes, each meeting reduced to just a couple of neat lines; an arrow shows a new short line being added after the meeting that just ended. On the right, a retired resident (about 70, white kurta, walking stick, hand raised) asks a question, his speech bubble showing a parking sign and a question mark; the secretary's register in reply shows only a tiny note with a parking sign and nothing more, and she shrugs slightly. Beside the register, one line is underlined in red with a small warning dot, hinting a slip got written in permanently. Soft evening tubelight, everyday community mood. Labels: "FULL HISTORY" on the dusty stack, "SUMMARY MEMORY" on the slim register, "DETAIL LOST" next to the resident's question.

key: A detective in a Byomkesh Bakshi story:
name: ch07_detective_react_loop
alt: A classic detective in a dhoti cycles through thinking, checking a railway register, and noting what he observes, shown as a loop.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of an old-world Kolkata-style setting split into three areas connected by a circular looping arrow. TOP LEFT: a thoughtful detective in his 40s (white dhoti and kurta, shawl over one shoulder, neatly combed hair, a calm sharp gaze) sits on a cane chair in a high-ceilinged study, chin resting on his hand, a thought bubble showing a servant with a clock reading 9. RIGHT: the same detective standing at a railway booking office window, running his finger down a big ledger handed over by a station clerk in a black coat. BOTTOM: the detective writes in a small notebook on a wooden table under a lamp, the notebook showing a tiny train ticket sketch and the time "8:50". From the notebook, a new curved arrow leads back to the top-left study, closing the loop, and a new thought bubble now shows a cook with a question mark. Each stage has a simple icon: a lightbulb, a magnifying glass, an eye. A pinned scratchpad on the wall behind collects all notes from earlier cycles. Muted sepia-tinted daylight, thoughtful mystery mood. Labels: "THOUGHT" near the study, "ACTION" near the booking window, "OBSERVATION" near the notebook.

key: A kirana shopkeeper who has worked there
name: ch08_cold_remedy_vs_cold_drink
alt: An experienced shopkeeper hands a customer ginger, honey and tablets for a cold, while a new helper brings a cold drink bottle.
scene: A wide, eye-level view across the counter of a cramped Indian kirana shop. In the centre stands a customer (woman in her 30s, shawl wrapped around her, red nose, tissue in hand) who has just said she needs something for a cold; her speech bubble shows a sneezing face. On the LEFT, the veteran shopkeeper (about 60, grey hair, sleeveless sweater, gentle smile) is placing a knob of ginger, a small jar of honey and a strip of tablets on the counter in front of her, none of which carry the word she said; soft glowing lines link her speech bubble to each item by meaning. On the RIGHT, a teenage new helper (about 17, oversized t-shirt, eager) proudly holds up a chilled glass bottle of fizzy drink pulled from a fridge with a big label showing a snowflake; a thin line links only the word on her bubble to the identical word on the bottle label, and the customer stares at it with a dismayed face. Shelves of jars, spices and soaps fill the background. In a small inset in the upper corner, the same veteran shopkeeper looks confused standing in an unfamiliar hardware shop, hinting the skill does not transfer. Warm tubelight, gently comic mood. Labels: "SEMANTIC SEARCH" above the veteran, "KEYWORD SEARCH" above the new helper.

key: Cutting a long train into coaches. Cut e
name: ch08_train_coach_chunking
alt: A long train shown cut two ways: sliced every few metres through passengers, versus cut neatly at the coach joints with a shared vestibule.
scene: A side-on, wide panoramic view of a long Indian passenger train parked at a quiet platform, shown twice, one above the other, separated by a thin horizontal line. TOP strip: giant dashed scissor lines cut the train at perfectly regular intervals measured by a big tape measure, slicing straight through windows and through passengers who are drawn split in half comically, with startled faces and a suitcase cut in two; the pieces drift slightly apart. BOTTOM strip: the same train is cut cleanly at the coupling joints between coaches, each coach whole with passengers sitting comfortably at windows, and between two coaches the shared vestibule is highlighted with a soft glow where a chai vendor (about 40, holding a kettle and paper cups) stands, a dotted bracket showing he belongs to both neighbouring coaches. A railway worker in orange overalls with a big wrench gives a thumbs-up beside the bottom strip, while a puzzled worker with giant scissors scratches his head beside the top strip. Clear late-morning light, tidy and slightly humorous mood. Labels: "FIXED SIZE" at the left of the top strip, "SENTENCE CHUNKS" at the left of the bottom strip, "OVERLAP" over the glowing vestibule.

key: Matching a lost-and-found description. A
name: ch08_lost_and_found_clerks
alt: Split image: a lost-and-found clerk comparing a description to pre-written tags versus a careful clerk holding the description beside each item.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, the same railway lost-and-found office in both halves with shelves of bags, umbrellas and suitcases. LEFT panel: a brisk clerk in his 40s (khaki shirt, spectacles pushed up) stands at a wall of small paper tags pinned in rows, one for every item on the shelves; he holds a customer's written slip in one hand and quickly runs his finger across the tags, matching words, with many fast arrows sweeping across the wall. One tag he picks shows a red bag with a black zip, close but wrong. RIGHT panel: a careful older clerk (about 60, white hair, cardigan, magnifying glass) holds the customer's written slip in one hand and an actual black bag with a red zip in the other, comparing them side by side, a small tick appearing between them; a short queue of only three items waits on his desk while a wall clock shows closing time approaching. The customer, a young woman with a backpack, waits anxiously at the counter in both halves. Even, slightly dusty office light. Labels: "BI-ENCODER" at the top of the left panel, "CROSS-ENCODER" at the top of the right panel, "SHORTLIST" beside the three items on the right-hand desk.

key: An open-book exam versus a closed-book e
name: ch08_open_book_exam
alt: Split image: a closed-book exam where a student writes a confident guess, versus an open-book exam where the student finds the right page and cites it.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, the same college exam hall and the same student (about 20, simple t-shirt, short hair, pen in hand) in both halves. LEFT panel: the desk is bare except for the answer sheet; the student writes fast with a confident grin, but his thought bubble shows a foggy, half-remembered page with smudged lines and a question mark; a small, wrong answer appears on his sheet circled lightly. RIGHT panel: a thick textbook lies open on his desk; his finger rests on one highlighted paragraph on page 47, a curved arrow carries the key fact from the book to his answer sheet, where he writes it in his own handwriting and adds a small bracket reference reading "p.47"; his expression is calm and certain. In the background of both panels, an invigilator walks between rows of desks under ceiling fans. A tiny inset in the lower right of the right panel shows the same student with the book open on the wrong page, a hint that retrieval must be right. Bright, even classroom light. Labels: "CLOSED BOOK" at the top of the left panel, "RETRIEVAL" beside the open textbook, "GROUNDED ANSWER" beside the answer sheet on the right.

key: A jigsaw puzzle of a Taj Mahal poster. O
name: ch09_jigsaw_patches
alt: A poster of a white marble monument cut into nine square jigsaw tiles, laid in order like coaches of a train being read from engine to guard van.
scene: A clean, slightly elevated view of a wooden table on which a poster of a famous white marble domed monument with minarets has been cut into nine perfect square tiles. On the left, the tiles lie scattered and jumbled, each one meaningless alone: a scrap of dome, a corner of sky, part of a minaret, a patch of garden; one tile is held up by a small girl (about 8, braids, school pinafore) who frowns at it in confusion. On the right, the same nine tiles are laid out in a single straight row like coaches of a train, with a small toy engine at the front and a guard van at the back, each tile carrying a small numbered position tag from 1 to 9; above the row, a ghosted faint outline of the full monument appears, as if the picture is reassembling in the viewer's mind. The girl's older brother (about 14, t-shirt, glasses) points along the row from left to right with a pencil. A small arrow shows the reading direction. Soft daylight from a window, quiet learning mood. Labels: "PATCHES" above the scattered tiles, "POSITION" beside the numbered tags, "VIT" above the row of tiles.

key: A school sports day "find your partner"
name: ch09_find_your_partner_game
alt: A school sports-day game where children holding photos and children holding caption cards are nudged by a teacher to pair up.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of a sunny school playground on sports day, with bunting strung between trees and white chalk lines on the grass. A dozen children in house-coloured t-shirts are scattered across the field; half hold large picture cards (a dog, a mango, a bicycle, a kite) and the other half hold matching caption cards drawn as a short line of scribbles beside a tiny matching icon. A cheerful PE teacher (woman in her 30s, track suit, whistle around her neck, cap) walks among them, gently steering a boy holding the dog picture toward a girl holding the dog caption, with a soft curved arrow pulling them together, while she waves a wrong pair apart with a small arrow pushing outward. Pairs that have already found each other stand side by side, grinning and holding hands; a few unmatched children wander looking at others' cards. In the upper corner, a small inset shows the same field from above as a dot map, matched pairs as dots touching. Bright morning sunlight, joyful, energetic mood. Labels: "IMAGE" above the picture-card holders, "TEXT" above the caption-card holders, "CONTRASTIVE" beside the teacher's arrows.

key: A brilliant blind professor (the LLM) an
name: ch09_blind_professor_interpreter
alt: A blind professor and a sharp-eyed assistant who speak different languages, connected by an interpreter passing glowing message tokens.
scene: A wide, eye-level view of an old university study with tall bookshelves and a large window looking onto a garden. On the RIGHT, a brilliant elderly professor (about 70, white beard, dark glasses, tweed jacket, holding a cane) sits in a leather armchair, head tilted, listening intently, surrounded by stacks of books. On the LEFT, a sharp-eyed young assistant (about 25, kurta, short hair, binoculars around her neck) stands at the window pointing out at a scene in the garden: a dog chasing a red ball under a mango tree. Between them sits a small, neat interpreter (about 40, waistcoat, headphones, a notepad) who listens to the assistant and then passes a short row of glowing coloured beads, not words, along a little tray to the professor's hand; the professor touches them and smiles in understanding. Speech bubbles from the assistant show strange symbols, meaning a different language. Above the beads, a tiny note shows they are not readable words. Warm afternoon window light, scholarly but warm mood. Labels: "IMAGE ENCODER" above the assistant, "Q-FORMER" above the interpreter, "LLM" above the professor.

key: Fitting a long wedding-hall group photo
name: ch09_squeezed_group_photo
alt: A long wedding group photo squeezed into a square frame so everybody looks tall and thin, with an uncle's turban distorted.
scene: A clean, front-on composition with two images side by side on a pale wall like framed prints. LEFT: a long, wide wedding group photograph in landscape format, about twenty relatives standing in two rows in front of a decorated stage with marigold garlands, the bride and groom in the centre, a jovial uncle in a bright saffron turban on the end, everyone with natural proportions and wide smiles. A curved arrow with two inward-pointing clamps leads from it to the RIGHT image: the same photo forced into a small square frame, every person stretched tall and pencil-thin, faces elongated, the stage narrowed, and the uncle's turban squashed into a tall narrow tower. A young couple (late 20s, casual clothes) stands in front of the square print, the woman laughing and pointing at the stretched uncle while the man counts heads on his fingers, showing the count is still easy. A small inset magnifier over the turban shows it tilted and warped. Soft gallery lighting, gently humorous mood. Labels: "ORIGINAL" under the long photo, "224 x 224" under the square photo, "DISTORTION" beside the magnifier.

key: A wedding matchmaker (cross-encoder) who
name: ch10_matchmaker_vs_biodata
alt: Split image: a matchmaker personally meeting two families for every pairing versus quickly comparing one-page biodata sheets.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a busy, slightly overwhelmed matchmaker aunty (about 55, silk saree, big bindi, reading glasses, diary under her arm) sits between two families on sofas in a crowded drawing room, sipping tea and studying how they interact; behind her stretches an endless queue of more families waiting at the door, winding out into the street, and a wall calendar shows months crossed off. A small counter in the corner shows a huge number of meetings. RIGHT panel: the same matchmaker now sits relaxed at a tidy desk, with neat one-page biodata sheets, each with a small photo and a few lines, laid out in a grid; she slides two sheets side by side and compares them in a glance, a quick tick appearing between them, a stack of processed sheets already filed. A small faint inset near the sheets shows two families laughing together, with a thought cloud noting what a sheet cannot capture. Warm domestic light on the left, clean bright office light on the right. Labels: "CROSS-ENCODER" at the top of the left panel, "BI-ENCODER" at the top of the right panel, "EMBEDDING" on one of the biodata sheets.

key: Tuning a tanpura: each string (pair) has
name: ch10_tanpura_tuning
alt: A musician tunes a tanpura by turning its pegs until each string's sound matches a target pitch.
scene: A close, slightly elevated three-quarter view of a classical music room with a cotton durrie on the floor, a framed portrait of a veena on the wall and incense smoke curling up. A young musician (about 25, white kurta, long hair tied back, focused expression) sits cross-legged with a tall tanpura resting upright against her shoulder, one hand twisting a wooden peg at the top while the other plucks a string. Beside her on the floor, a small electronic tuner shows a needle approaching a centre mark. Floating to the right of the tanpura are four small cards, one per string, each showing two sound-wave lines: a dashed target wave and a solid current wave, nearly aligned on some cards and further apart on others. Thin connecting lines run from every peg to every string card, showing that turning one peg slightly shifts all the waves at once. A soft glow surrounds the card that has just matched. In the background, her teacher (an elderly man with a shawl) listens with closed eyes. Warm, golden lamp light, serene concentration. Labels: "TARGET LABEL" beside the dashed waves, "COSINE" on the tuner display, "WEIGHTS" next to the pegs.

key: Training a bank's fraud checker on fake
name: ch10_signature_hard_negatives
alt: A bank fraud checker being trained on three fakes of a customer's signature: a child's scribble, another person's signature, and a skilled forgery.
scene: A wide, eye-level view of a quiet back room in an Indian bank with a wooden desk, a desk lamp, a stamp pad and a steel cupboard. A trainee fraud checker (about 26, white shirt, tie, earnest face) sits with a magnifying glass, while a senior manager (about 55, grey waistcoat, spectacles) stands behind him pointing. On the desk, a genuine signature card of a customer sits at the top centre with a green tick. Below it, laid in a row from left to right, are three fake cards: a child's crayon scribble, obviously wrong, that the trainee barely glances at; a neat signature of a completely different name, which makes him pause; and a near-perfect forgery of the customer's own signature that he is studying closely under the magnifying glass, sweat on his brow. Small difficulty meters above each card rise from low to high. Off to the side, a fourth card that is actually genuine sits in the forgery pile with a warning triangle, hinting at a mislabeled example. Warm lamp light in a dim room, tense, careful mood. Labels: "EASY NEGATIVE" above the scribble, "HARD NEGATIVE" above the skilled forgery, "ANCHOR" beside the genuine card.

key: A telegram with half the words missing (
name: ch10_telegram_reconstruct
alt: A telegraph clerk reads a telegram with most words missing and writes the full letter back from a single idea in his head.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of an old Indian telegraph office counter: wooden partitions, a brass telegraph key, rolls of paper tape and a big wall clock. On the left, a strip of telegram paper is pinned to the counter, with only three words printed in capitals, "ARRIVING TRAIN FRIDAY", and wide blank gaps between them. In the centre, a thoughtful clerk (about 45, spectacles, sleeve garters, neat moustache) reads the strip; above his head floats a single small glowing card holding a simple picture, a smiling traveller with a suitcase stepping off a train under a calendar marked Friday, representing one compact idea. From that card a flowing arrow leads to the right, where his hand writes a full, long letter on cream paper with many lines of handwriting, carefully reconstructed. The original sender, a young man with a small bag, waits outside the window looking hopeful. The clerk never looks back at the telegram once writing starts; a small eye icon with a cross near it shows he works only from the card. Soft dusty light through high windows, quiet, nostalgic mood. Labels: "NOISY INPUT" beside the gappy telegram, "EMBEDDING" on the glowing card, "DECODER" beside the writing hand.

key: A cricket team where the batting coach (
name: ch11_coach_frozen_vs_trainable
alt: Split image: a batting coach can only move a batter whose technique is locked, versus a coach whose feedback reshapes the batter's grip and footwork.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves in the same cricket nets with green netting, a concrete pitch and a bowling machine at the far end. LEFT panel: a young batter (about 19, white kit, helmet, pads) stands stiffly, his body outlined with a faint padlock-shaped glow and small chain links around his arms and feet; the coach (about 50, track jacket, cap, whistle) can only push the whole batter sideways on a marked spot on the crease, a straight sideways arrow showing the only allowed change, the coach looking limited and patient. RIGHT panel: the same batter is free, no glow; the coach crouches beside him adjusting his grip on the bat handle, with small curved arrows showing changes to his front foot, wrist angle and timing, and a ball being struck cleanly off the middle with a satisfying crack lines. A small inset in the corner shows every muscle of the batter lit up by tiny arrows, hinting that every part gets nudged. Bright afternoon sun, practice-session mood. Labels: "FROZEN" at the top of the left panel, "TRAINABLE" at the top of the right panel, "HEAD" beside the coach in the left panel.

key: A railway ticket checker learning to tel
name: ch11_ticket_checker_pairs
alt: A train ticket checker learns to tell first-class from sleeper passengers by comparing pairs, then draws a simple line to sort them.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of a railway platform with a long train on one side. A ticket checker (woman in her 30s, black coat, name badge, notebook in hand, sharp observant eyes) stands at the centre. In front of her, passengers are brought up in pairs: on the left, two well-dressed travellers with leather suitcases standing together with a green link between them meaning same class; on the right, a well-dressed traveller next to a passenger with a cloth bundle and a steel trunk, with a red broken link meaning different class. Behind, a long queue of more pairs waits, a tally on a board showing many comparisons made from only a few people. Above the checker floats an inset showing a simple map of dots where the two classes have separated into two clouds with a straight line drawn between them. At the far right, she now confidently waves new passengers toward the correct coach doors without needing pairs. Bright morning platform light with pigeons and a tea stall, busy but orderly mood. Labels: "SAME CLASS" beside the green-linked pair, "DIFFERENT CLASS" beside the red-linked pair, "SETFIT" above the inset with the line.

key: A general physician who joins a cardiolo
name: ch11_doctor_reads_case_files
alt: A general physician new to a cardiology hospital spends a month quietly reading the hospital's heart case files before triaging ECG reports.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of a hospital records room turned reading room: tall metal racks of files, a window showing a hospital courtyard with an ambulance, and a large wall poster of a heart. In the centre, a young general physician (about 30, white coat, stethoscope around her neck, hair in a bun) sits at a long table surrounded by stacks of cardiology case files, reading intently with a highlighter, a cup of tea going cold beside her; small floating word clouds around her show heart, ECG wave and valve icons, as if she is soaking up the vocabulary. A wall calendar shows a full month of days crossed off. No marks or grades appear anywhere on the files. On the right, through a glass door, the next stage is visible: the same doctor at a desk triaging a pile of ECG printouts into two trays with a confident expression. Behind her, a small framed medical-school degree hangs on the wall, faint and slightly faded, hinting older general knowledge can fade if this goes on too long. Soft clinical daylight, quiet studious mood. Labels: "CONTINUED PRETRAINING" above the reading table, "FINE-TUNING" over the glass door to the triage room.

key: Sentiment classification is a teacher wr
name: ch11_grade_vs_highlighter
alt: Split image: a teacher writing one grade on top of an essay versus a teacher highlighting names, places and companies word by word.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, the same teacher (woman in her 40s, cotton saree, spectacles on a chain, kind but exacting) at the same wooden staffroom desk in both halves, the same handwritten essay in front of her. LEFT panel: she writes one large circled grade at the top of the page in red ink, a confident single stroke, and the rest of the page is untouched; a small speech bubble from her shows a smiley face meaning positive. RIGHT panel: she holds three highlighter pens fanned in one hand, green, blue and purple, and has gone through the essay word by word: a person's name glows green, a city name glows blue, a company name glows purple, with tiny matching icons (a face, a map pin, a building) in the margin beside each line. One long name is shown split into three small highlighted pieces joined by a tiny bracket, hinting that sub-word pieces must be stitched back together. A stack of essays and a bell sit at the edge of the desk. Bright staffroom window light, focused academic mood. Labels: "CLASSIFICATION" at the top of the left panel, "NER" at the top of the right panel, "TOKENS" beside the split name.

key: A mixer-grinder with interchangeable jar
name: ch12_mixer_grinder_jars
alt: A mixer-grinder motor base with interchangeable jars for chutney, dry masala and juice, one jar being swapped on.
scene: A close, slightly elevated three-quarter view of a granite kitchen counter in an Indian home, morning light through a window with a tulsi plant on the sill. In the centre sits the heavy white motor base of a mixer-grinder, solid and immovable, with a small padlock icon on its side to show it never changes. A woman in her 40s (cotton nightie with a dupatta, hair tied up, practised hands) is lifting a small chutney jar full of green coriander chutney off the base and is about to fit a tall juice jar of orange pulp onto the coupling; a curved swap arrow arcs between the two. Lined up on the counter to the right are two more jars ready to go: a small steel dry-masala jar with whole spices and a medium jar with soaked rice for dosa batter, each with a small coloured ring on its base. To the left, a jar from a different appliance with a clearly mismatched square coupling sits with a red cross over it, showing it does not fit this motor. Bowls of coconut, chillies and oranges are scattered around. Bright, fresh morning light, homely, efficient mood. Labels: "FROZEN BASE MODEL" on the motor base, "ADAPTERS" above the row of jars, "WRONG BASE" beside the mismatched jar.

key: Writing corrections on sticky notes in a
name: ch12_sticky_notes_reprint
alt: Corrections written on sticky notes in a textbook, then reprinted into a clean new edition, with the sticky-note file kept aside.
scene: A clean, slightly elevated view of a long wooden desk, laid out left to right as a small sequence. LEFT: an open, well-used textbook with several bright yellow sticky notes stuck on its pages, each with a short handwritten correction and an arrow pointing at a line of print; a teacher (about 50, half-sleeve shirt, pen in hand, reading glasses) is adding one more note. CENTRE: a small printing press with a crank, a fresh sheet sliding out, and an arrow showing the sticky-note corrections flowing into the printed page; the corrections now appear as normal typed text with no notes attached. RIGHT: a crisp new edition of the book with a ribbon on the cover marked "2nd ed.", a student (about 18, t-shirt, backpack) reading it happily with no sticky notes in sight. In the foreground, slightly apart, a small labelled envelope holds the original sticky notes, kept safe, with a small curved arrow showing they could be applied to a different book instead. Warm desk-lamp light and soft daylight, tidy, productive mood. Labels: "ADAPTER" beside the sticky notes, "MERGE" over the printing press, "MERGED MODEL" beside the new edition.

key: An eye test at the optician: "Is it clea
name: ch12_eye_test_lens_choice
alt: At an optician's, a person easily answers whether lens one or lens two is clearer, while a separate scale of 1 to 10 leaves them puzzled.
scene: A close, eye-level view inside a small Indian optician's shop with a letter chart glowing on the far wall and frames displayed in glass cabinets. A middle-aged man (about 45, checked shirt, balding, earnest) sits in an examination chair with a heavy metal trial frame on his face. The optometrist (woman in her 30s, white coat, hair tied back, friendly) stands beside him holding up two round lenses, one in each hand, labelled "1" and "2" on little tabs. A speech bubble from the man shows him pointing confidently toward lens 2, with a clear check mark. Above him, a faint second thought bubble shows a ruler-like scale from 1 to 10 with a large question mark and a sweating face, showing how hard it would be to give an absolute score. On the right, a small clipboard on the counter shows a simple list of pairs, one side of each pair ticked. In a small inset in the corner, two other customers point at different lenses for the same pair, hinting that people disagree. Dim room with the bright letter chart glowing, calm, clinical mood. Labels: "PREFERENCE PAIR" above the two lenses, "CHOSEN" beside lens 2, "NO ABSOLUTE SCORE" beside the faint scale bubble.

key: Instead of hiring a separate food critic
name: ch12_cook_compares_yesterday
alt: A cook compares today's cooking with a video of yesterday's, shifting toward the dish customers chose and away from the one sent back.
scene: A wide, eye-level view of a small restaurant kitchen with steel counters, a tandoor glowing in the corner and hanging ladles. In the centre, a young cook (about 28, white chef's jacket, bandana, focused) stands at the stove stirring a pot. Mounted on the wall beside him, a tablet plays a video of himself cooking the same dish yesterday, the image slightly faded and unchanging, with a small pause icon. On the counter to his left sit two plates from customers: one returned plate with an untouched oily curry and a red cross card, one clean plate wiped spotless with a green tick card. Arrows show the cook leaning slightly toward the green-ticked style and away from the red-crossed one, compared against yesterday's video, as if he is asking himself whether he is now more likely to make the chosen dish than before. Notably absent is any food critic: an empty chair by the door has a small sign with a crossed-out magnifying glass. A small balance-beam icon floats above the cook between the video and the plates. Warm, steamy kitchen light, determined mood. Labels: "REFERENCE MODEL" on the wall tablet, "CHOSEN" beside the clean plate, "REJECTED" beside the returned plate.

key: Finishing a long train journey from Delh
name: ch13_delhi_to_chennai_journey
alt: A long train journey across India seen through a window, each station showing a different landscape, with a conductor thanking the passenger at the end.
scene: A wide panoramic view designed like a long horizontal journey, read left to right. A long blue passenger train winds across the frame through changing scenery: on the far left a busy northern city platform with red sandstone buildings and a chai stall, then golden wheat fields, then rocky central plateaus with a fort on a hill, then a river bridge, then green coconut palms and paddy fields, and on the far right a southern terminus station with a temple tower in the distance and the sea beyond. Along the track, small station signboards mark the stops, each showing only a chapter number from 1 to 12 instead of a name. In the foreground, framed by an open train window, a young passenger (late 20s, kurta, backpack, notebook in hand) leans out, eyes wide, looking back at all the landscapes. At the far right, a conductor in a black coat smiles and tips his cap, and the rails beyond the terminus continue faintly into the horizon instead of ending, hinting that the field keeps going. Warm golden-hour light, reflective, satisfied mood. Labels: "CHAPTERS" above the row of station signboards, "NO TERMINUS" beside the rails fading into the horizon.

key: Learning to run a kirana shop. First you
name: ch13_kirana_three_stages
alt: Three panels of learning to run a kirana shop: learning the till, serving from stock, and making a house-brand masala.
scene: A three-panel illustration in a horizontal row separated by thin vertical lines, the same young shopkeeper (about 24, checked shirt, apron, eager) in the same small kirana shop in all three. LEFT panel: he stands behind the counter with an older mentor (about 60, white kurta, spectacles) who is opening the drawer of an old cash till and pointing at labelled shelves, the young man taking notes in a small diary. MIDDLE panel: the young man serves a smiling customer (a woman with a cloth bag) from packets already on the shelves, handing over rice and soap, comfortable and quick. RIGHT panel: he grinds spices in a small mortar and pestle on the counter and fills clear jars with his own house-brand masala, hand-labelled with a little star logo, while a neighbour sniffs a jar and nods approvingly. In the corner of the right panel, a delivery man is wheeling in a shiny new cash till, hinting that the base keeps changing. Warm, friendly daylight throughout. Labels: "HOW LLMS WORK" at the top of the left panel, "PRETRAINED MODELS" at the top of the middle panel, "FINE-TUNING" at the top of the right panel.

key: Getting a driving licence. The test prov
name: ch13_licence_then_real_roads
alt: A new driver holding a licence at a test track, then driving on a busy real road where signs and routes keep changing.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a quiet driving test ground with orange cones, a painted reverse-parking bay and a small slope; a young woman (about 23, kurta and jeans, hair tied back, proud smile) stands beside a small white hatchback holding up a freshly issued driving licence card, while an examiner in a khaki uniform ticks a clipboard. RIGHT panel: the same young woman now drives the same hatchback on a busy Indian city road: auto-rickshaws, buses, a cow at the roadside, scooters weaving; overhead, a workman on a ladder is replacing a road sign with a new one, a fresh diversion board stands in the lane, and a phone mounted on her dashboard shows a navigation route that has just redrawn itself with a looping arrow. She is concentrating, hands at ten and two, learning as she goes. A small calendar icon near the new road sign flips pages quickly, hinting the rules change in months. Calm overcast light on the left, bright busy midday light on the right. Labels: "THE BOOK" at the top of the left panel, "THE FIELD" at the top of the right panel, "KEEPS CHANGING" beside the new road sign.

key: Net practice before a cricket match: the
name: ch13_nets_random_deliveries
alt: A batter in cricket nets facing random deliveries from a bowling machine, with chapter cards flashing as each ball arrives.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of floodlit cricket practice nets in the evening, green netting on three sides and a bowling machine at the far end. A young batter (about 26, office shirt sleeves rolled under batting pads and a helmet, determined face) stands at the crease mid-shot. The bowling machine, operated by a grinning friend in a t-shirt, fires balls at different heights and angles, each shown with a curved path: one bouncer, one yorker, one wide outswinger. Floating beside each incoming ball is a small card with a chapter number on it, so each delivery is a random question and the batter must recall the matching chapter on the spot; one card glows as the batter connects cleanly. On a bench at the side, a coach in a tracksuit (about 50, whistle) holds a clipboard and gestures as if adding a follow-up question, with a small speech bubble showing a question mark and a branching arrow, like an interviewer adjusting to the answer. A water bottle and a kit bag lie on the grass. Bright floodlights against a deep blue evening sky, focused, competitive mood. Labels: "RANDOM QUESTIONS" above the incoming balls, "RECALL" beside the batter, "FOLLOW-UP" beside the coach's speech bubble.
